usage: fleet-switchboard launch [-h] [--agent AGENT] [--dir DIR]
                                [--resume SESSION] [--headless] [--terminal]
                                [--workspace WORKSPACE] [--role ROLE]
                                [--reports-to REPORTS_TO] [--issue ISSUE]
                                [--repo REPO] [--new-workspace LABEL]
                                [--charter CHARTER] [--checkpoint WHEN]
                                [--overdue WHEN] [--brief-file BRIEF_FILE]
                                [--memory-ok REASON] [--cloud]
                                [--branch BRANCH] [--idle IDLE] [--hard HARD]
                                [--shape SHAPE] [--stack]
                                name

Start a fleet agent (headless by default, or in a new herdr tab with
--terminal), without typing. A NEW launch (not a resume or --cloud) first runs
the memory test: this is the lanes' safety check, not the owner's rule (there
are no caps on coders), and `--memory-ok <reason>` overrides it. A refusal
exits 5.

positional arguments:
  name                  The agent's fleet name (lower case, digits, - and _)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --agent AGENT         The OpenCode agent definition, such as coder
  --dir DIR             The agent's working directory (absolute)
  --resume SESSION      Open a tab on this existing session of NAME instead of
                        creating one (a restart that keeps the conversation)
  --headless            Start the worker with NO terminal: a session in the
                        OpenCode service, the brief sent through the API
                        (about 2 MB instead of a terminal's 200 to 400 MB).
                        Its tools run in the service's environment. The
                        default of a plain launch (see --terminal); unlike the
                        default, an explicit --headless never falls back to a
                        terminal
  --terminal            Open a herdr tab for the worker (a plain launch is
                        headless unless the configuration key launch_default
                        is terminal). Cannot be combined with --headless;
                        --workspace and --new-workspace imply it
  --workspace WORKSPACE
                        The herdr workspace for the new tab (default: the
                        workspace of this session, else $HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID)
  --role ROLE           metadata.fleet.role
  --reports-to REPORTS_TO
                        metadata.fleet.reports_to
  --issue ISSUE         metadata.fleet.issue (owner/repo#N also sets --repo)
  --repo REPO           metadata.fleet.repo, OWNER/REPO: the project the agent
                        works in. Its gh account (config gh_users) is the
                        agent's GH_TOKEN
  --new-workspace LABEL
                        Create a herdr workspace with this label in --dir
                        (never focused), and launch into it. A --charter whose
                        `workspace:` line differs is refused
  --charter CHARTER     metadata.fleet.charter: an orchestrator's charter
                        issue
  --checkpoint WHEN     Remind the worker to report at this time (30m, or an
                        ISO time with a zone). Default: read from the brief's
                        CHECKPOINT line, if it can be
  --overdue WHEN        Wake --reports-to at this time if the worker has not
                        reported since the launch (60m, or an ISO time with a
                        zone)
  --brief-file BRIEF_FILE
                        The first prompt: a file, or - for stdin
  --memory-ok REASON    Skip the memory test of a new launch (audited with the
                        reason)
  --cloud               Run the worker in the cloud (needs --repo and
                        --branch; --dir is its path in the pod, default /work;
                        the pod always runs its own 'worker' agent: --agent is
                        only recorded)
  --branch BRANCH       With --cloud: the branch the worker starts on
  --idle IDLE           With --cloud: stop after this long idle (default 10m)
  --hard HARD           With --cloud: stop after this long whatever it does
                        (default 2h)
  --shape SHAPE         With --cloud: the pod shape, S (2 CPU, 4 GiB; the
                        launcher's default) or M (4 CPU, 8 GiB)
  --stack               With --cloud: a pod that can run a nested Docker stack
                        (the Sysbox runtime class, its own user namespace, no
                        capability added, no privileged mode). Off by default;
                        the launch without it is unchanged. The first pod on a
                        fresh node may wait for the node's runtime: the
                        launcher retries
